question: What is considered a primary focus of injection safety in nursing practice?

options.A: Administering injections as quickly as possible to save time
options.B: A holistic chain of events from hand hygiene to safe sharps disposal
options.C: Reusing syringes only when patients request it
options.D: Focusing solely on the correct dosage of the medication

explanation: Injection safety encompasses a holistic chain of events starting from hand hygiene and skin prep to sterile equipment use and safe sharps disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h1)

question: Why is injection safety particularly emphasized in nursing education?

options.A: To ensure students learn how to manufacture syringes
options.B: To prevent nurses from ever having to administer injections
options.C: To protect patients and healthcare workers from preventable healthcare-associated infections
options.D: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene before procedures

explanation: Nursing education instills rigorous safety habits early to protect patients, staff, and the community from preventable harm caused by unsafe practices. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h1)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what characterizes a safe injection?

options.A: It is administered quickly and uses the cheapest available equipment
options.B: It does not harm the recipient, avoids risks to the worker, and creates no dangerous community waste
options.C: It is performed only by senior physicians
options.D: It involves reusing multi-dose vials indefinitely

explanation: A safe injection by WHO standards protects the recipient, exposes the healthcare worker to no avoidable risks, and produces safe waste. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h2)

question: Which of the following best describes the consequence of an accidental versus an intentional unsafe injection practice?

options.A: Accidental breaches do not transmit infections
options.B: Intentional breaches are more harmful than accidental ones
options.C: The biological consequences and infection risks remain identical regardless of intent
options.D: Accidental breaches only affect the nurse

explanation: Whether a breach in safety is intentional or accidental, the biological consequences and infection risks are identical. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why is changing only the needle while reusing the same syringe between patients considered unsafe?

options.A: Syringes are too expensive to reuse safely
options.B: The syringe barrel or plunger can remain contaminated with blood and pathogens
options.C: It takes too much time during a busy shift
options.D: Needles cannot be detached from syringes

explanation: Reusing a syringe even with a new needle can transmit pathogens because the body of the syringe often becomes contaminated during use. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is a major risk associated with improper handling of multi-dose medication vials?

options.B: Microorganisms can contaminate the vial and infect subsequent patients
options.C: The vial glass will shatter easily

explanation: Entering a multi-dose vial with contaminated equipment allows microorganisms to enter and contaminate the medication for future users. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is a frequent systemic cause of unsafe injection practices in resource-constrained settings?

options.B: Stockouts of disposable syringes and safety equipment
options.C: An excess number of nursing staff on every shift

explanation: Stockouts of single-use syringes and safety devices often pressure staff to improvise or reuse items. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h4)

question: How do patient perceptions sometimes contribute to unsafe injection volumes?

options.A: Patients refuse all forms of medication
options.B: Patients demand oral medications instead of injections
options.C: Patients may believe injections are superior, increasing the demand for unnecessary procedures
options.D: Patients insist on bringing their own sterile syringes

explanation: Cultural beliefs favoring injectables can drive a high demand for unnecessary injections, raising overall procedural risks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do unsafe injections transmit blood-borne pathogens so efficiently?

options.A: Injections are always performed in sterile operating rooms
options.B: Needles bypass external barriers like skin, delivering pathogens directly into circulation
options.C: Viruses cannot survive outside the human body
options.D: Pathogens are neutralized by subcutaneous tissue

explanation: Accessing blood vessels directly bypasses natural skin barriers, introducing infectious agents straight into the systemic circulation. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h5)

question: Among the major blood-borne pathogens, which one typically carries the highest risk of transmission following a contaminated needlestick injury?
explanation: Hepatitis B Virus carries the highest rate of transmission after a percutaneous exposure compared to HCV and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is a major consequence of unsafe injection practices on the Nigerian health system?

options.B: Increased morbidity, mortality, and strain from chronic infections like Hepatitis B and C
options.C: The complete eradication of infectious diseases
options.D: A decreased demand for healthcare services

explanation: Unsafe injections drive up rates of chronic infections like Hepatitis and HIV, placing a heavy economic and clinical burden on the health system. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h6)

question: What type of devices are promoted by national policies to help curb unsafe injection practices in Nigeria?
explanation: National injection safety policies promote auto-disable syringes to prevent the intentional or accidental reuse of injection equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of the aseptic non-touch technique (ANTT) during injection preparation?

options.A: To speed up the medication administration process
options.B: To ensure key sterile parts do not touch unsterile surfaces or fingers
options.C: To eliminate the need for hand hygiene
options.D: To allow the reuse of syringe barrels

explanation: ANTT focuses on protecting key sterile parts of equipment from contact with unsterile surfaces or hands to prevent contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h7)

question: Which method is recommended if a needle must be recapped in an unavoidable clinical situation?

options.B: Holding the cap with bare fingers while inserting the needle
options.D: Blowing on the needle to cool it before recapping

explanation: The one-handed scoop technique prevents the healthcare worker's hand from being positioned in front of the exposed needle point, reducing needlestick risks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h7)

question: What ethical responsibility does a nurse have when observing a colleague engaging in unsafe injection practices?

options.A: Ignore the action to maintain workplace harmony
options.B: Record the incident on social media
options.C: Intervene, provide correction, and report through proper institutional channels
options.D: Imitate the colleague to save time during busy shifts

explanation: Nurses have an ethical duty to correct unsafe behaviors and report them properly to protect patient and staff safety. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h8)

question: How do nurses contribute to patient and community education regarding injections?

options.A: By encouraging patients to request injections for every minor ailment
options.B: By dispelling myths that every illness requires an injectable medication
options.C: By teaching patients how to self-administer intravenous drugs at home
options.D: By discouraging the use of oral medications entirely

explanation: Nurses educate patients to dispel the myth that injections are always superior, helping reduce unnecessary procedures and cumulative risks. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T1#GNS122_U4_T1_h8)
